s01.client_chat.cc_001: You don't know me. My name is Nora Ilves. I worked with Elias Rand.
s01.client_chat.cc_002: Seven weeks ago they found him at the bottom of the service stairwell at our office. The police wrote it up as a fall and closed it in eleven days.
s01.client_chat.cc_003: It wasn't a fall. He'd found something in our product — a flaw — and our CEO told him, in writing, that reporting it would end him.
s01.client_chat.cc_004: Four days later Elias was dead and the flaw was never filed.
s01.client_chat.cc_005: I recovered his phone. It is a company handset and I am the engineer who enrols them, so I did not have to ask anybody for it.
s01.client_chat.cc_006: I'm not asking you to like me. I'm asking you to read a dead man's phone and tell me what's in it.
s01.client_chat.cc_008: Good. Access is live. You're seeing that phone as it is right now, not as it was.
s01.client_chat.cc_009: Start with the last night. Tuesday, the fourth of March. Everything you need is in those six hours.
s01.interstitial.is1_001: That's him. That's the whole case, laid out like a receipt.
s01.interstitial.is1_002: Send me what you have and I'll walk it into the prosecutor's office myself tomorrow.
s01.interstitial.is1_003: You can stop now. Genuinely. There's nothing else in that phone.
s01.interstitial.is2_001: Why are you still in there.
s01.interstitial.is2_002: You were hired to find who killed Elias. Not to audit the edit history of a spreadsheet.
s01.closing_chat.cl_002: Seven weeks ago I killed a software architect and I hung a CEO for it. It was flawless.
s01.closing_chat.cl_003: The trouble with something flawless is that if no one ever sees it, it never happened at all.
s01.closing_chat.cl_004: So I hired someone who would see it. If I had simply announced it, I'd be one more liar on the internet. Nobody counts those.
s01.closing_chat.cl_005: You found my signature over my objections. That's why what you're holding isn't a claim. It's a finding.
s01.closing_chat.cl_006: Viktor was released this morning. Kilian took out a loan he can't repay because he couldn't afford to bury his brother. Help him, if you can. He did nothing.
s01.closing_chat.cl_007: I've attached your report to the file. It publishes at six. What do you do?
s01.closing_chat.cl_007.opt1: Take all of it to the police.
s01.closing_chat.cl_007.opt2: Strip my name off it before it publishes.
s01.closing_chat.cl_008: Good. On the record, verified, filed by a professional. That's the version that lasts.
s01.closing_chat.cl_009: They'll look for me. They won't find me. That part was arranged in January.
s01.closing_chat.cl_010: Ah. You understood the actual point.
s01.closing_chat.cl_011: Without your name on it, it's a confession from a ghost, and nobody has to believe a ghost. That was the one thing you could take from me. You took it.
s01.closing_chat.cl_013: Viktor walks free, Kilian stays ruined, and I am not here. The case is closed and no one alive knows it happened. I can live with that. Can you?
s01.closing_chat.cl_014: This account goes dark when you close this window. Thank you for the attention, detective. It was the whole point.
s01.messages.sms_001: I need 8000. I know how it sounds. It's the last time, I swear on Mum.
s01.messages.sms_002: I can't, Kilian. Not again. I'm sorry.
s01.messages.sms_003: You have it and you won't. Remember that you had a choice here.
s01.messages.sms_004: Forget I said that. I'm not in a good place. Please call me.
s01.messages.sms_005: I meant it about calling. I'm not angry. I just don't have anyone else.

s01.notes.note_020.title: Design notes — token refresh
s01.notes.note_020.block_001: The refresh path re-signs the assertion but never re-checks the subject. That's not a bug you introduce by accident; the check was there in build 39 and gone in build 41.
s01.notes.note_020.block_002: Whoever removed it also removed the test that would have caught it. Same commit. That's the part I can't explain away.
s01.notes.note_020.block_003: Options: (a) fix quietly, (b) fix loudly, (c) fix loudly and externally.
s01.notes.note_020.block_004: It has to be (c). If I do it quietly and it's deliberate, I've just told them which door to close and which to keep open.

s01.notes.note_021.block_002: Record it. He'll deny the wording afterwards, he always does.
s01.notes.note_021.block_003: Don't argue about the money. It's not about the round.
s01.notes.note_021.block_004: Say the word out loud. Make him respond to the word.

s01.memos.vm_013.title: Sunday
s01.memos.vm_013.transcript: It's Sunday evening and I've just spent two hours reading the same forty lines of code. I know what I'm going to do. I've known since Thursday. I'm just letting myself be scared about it for a few more days, which is fine, that's allowed. Tuesday I put it in front of him and then it's not mine alone any more. That's the part I actually want. Not being right. Just not being the only one who knows.

s01.memos.vm_015.title: After the design session
s01.memos.vm_015.transcript: Ben asked why we re-sign the assertion at refresh and the honest answer is that nobody has looked at it since 2019. Six years. Six years of "that's just how it works". Write the ADR. Not because anyone will read it, but because in three years someone else's Ben is going to ask, and they deserve a better answer than the one I just gave him.
s01.memos.vm_016.title: Airport, early
s01.memos.vm_016.transcript: Gate 14, nobody here, coffee machine broken. I like the airport at this hour. Everything is about to happen and nothing has yet.
s01.memos.vm_017.title: Tuesday
s01.memos.vm_017.transcript: Right. Tonight. Everything in one folder, the recording on, and I say the word out loud so it exists in a room with a witness in it. Worst case he fires me and I file it from outside, which is the same outcome with a worse coffee machine. Best case he does the right thing, which — let's be honest — I've stopped expecting. Either way it stops being only mine tonight. That's the part I actually want.

s01.question.q15.title: Name them
s01.question.q15.question: The badge log was forged at 06:12. The phone was backed up at 01:12, from a paired device, while Elias was already dead and no police had entered the building. Who killed Elias Rand?
s01.ending.police: Six weeks later the file goes in as evidence and NULLKEY is named in an indictment nobody can serve. Viktor Halme sues the state and wins. Kilian Rand gets a settlement that covers the loan and nothing else. Nora Ilves is never found — but she is on the record now, credited, permanent, exactly as she wanted, and that was the one thing she could not forge for herself.
s01.ending.erase: The report publishes at six with her name stripped out of it: a murder solved by an anonymous source who cannot be questioned. Prosecutors decline to act on a ghost. Viktor Halme keeps the acquittal and loses everything else, because the public never learns who to blame instead. Somewhere, a woman reads the coverage of her perfect crime and finds someone else's silence in the byline. She never contacts you again.
s01.ending.silence: Nothing publishes. Kilian Rand buries his brother on borrowed money and never learns who did it. Viktor Halme stays the man it probably was. The account goes dark on schedule, and the only two people alive who know what happened to Elias Rand are the woman who killed him and you.
